summary: String tokenizer: builds a 32-byte bit map of delimiter characters from a2, then scans a1 (or the thread-local default buffer at TLS+24) for the first character not in the set, advances to the next delimiter, truncates it with a NUL, and stores the new scan position back into TLS+24. Returns the token start, or 0 when no token is found.

local_names.a1: token buffer; when NULL the thread-local buffer at TLS+24 is used
local_names.a2: delimiter character string used to build the bitmap
local_names.v7: 32-byte bitmap with one bit per delimiter character

operations.description: v8 = TLSValueRetrievalWithInit() to obtain the thread-local state pointer.
For each character in a2 (until NUL), set its bit: v7[char >> 3] |= 1 << (char & 7).
v4 = a1; when a1 is NULL, v4 = the default pointer stored at TLS offset +24.
Read the current buffer character via a1/this and test whether its bit is set in v7 while the character is nonzero.
Advance v4 while the current character's bit is set in the delimiter bitmap and the character is not NUL (skips leading delimiters).
v5 = v4 records the start of the token.
Scan from v5: while *v4 != 0, if the current character's bit is set in the bitmap, write 0 there (truncate) and stop.
Store the final scan position back at TLS offset +24 so the next call continues after this token.
return v5 when a token was found (v4 != v5), otherwise return 0.

clean_pseudocode: do { v3 = *a2; v7[(unsigned char)*a2 >> 3] |= 1 << (*a2 & 7); ++a2; } while ( v3 );
while ( *v4 ) { if ( ((unsigned char)(1 << (*v4 & 7)) & v7[(unsigned char)*v4 >> 3]) != 0 ) { *v4++ = 0; break; } ++v4; }
unresolved: Semantics of the thread-local slot at TLS+24 (persistent tokenizer state buffer) unknown.
Cluster prelabel marks this as a structural twin of ConditionalFreeWithBit0Flag (00404f70); whether the twin shares this tokenizer semantics is unverified.
Behavior when the input buffer contains no delimiter is caller-dependent; return of 0 for empty token is assumed.
